name: 12 V supply · charge pump and regulator (78L12)
description: The TC1044S doubler (about 17.5 V on V18) with a 78L12 after it, holding V12 at 12 V (onsemi MC78L00A/D, Figure 2: 0.33 µF in, 0.1 µF out). Unlike a zener, it holds 12 V whatever the circuit draws, as long as V18 stays above 13.7 V (with 10 mA drawn it still sits at 16.5 V). The regulator takes 4.2 mA itself, from the pump. For a heavier load, pick an LT1054 in U1's settings. Label the stages it powers V12.

notes.part:U1: Doubler: V+ in, about 2 × V+ out. Pin 2 swings C2 between ground and V+, lifting the D1/D2 junction; pin 5 goes to ground. Supply: pin 8 is the chip's supply input, fed from the pedal's V+ (the DC jack or the battery, through the input filter). The pump draws its current in short pulses at its switching rate; a bulk electrolytic on V+ (10-100 µF, such as the Input filter block's 47 Ω and 100 µF) supplies them close by, so they don't travel back along V+ and whine in the other stages. A pedal that already has one on V+ needs no second cap here (one close to pin 8 helps a little on a long board). A pedal with none, such as a bare battery fuzz like the Rangemaster, needs one: the "Supply without a bulk capacitor" warning says so.
notes.part:C1: Reservoir: holds V18 up between the pump's pulses. Bigger means less ripple.
notes.net:V18: About 17.5 V from a 9 V supply: 2 × 9 V less two diode drops and the pump's output resistance.
notes.part:C2: Pump cap: the bigger, the lower the pump's output resistance (1/(f × C) of it).
notes.part:D1: D1 charges C2 from V+; D2 passes its charge on to V18. Schottkys (1N5817) drop the least.
notes.part:U2: 78L12: holds V12 at 12 V while V18 stays above about 13.7 V (12 V plus its 1.7 V dropout), up to 100 mA. It takes 4.2 mA itself, load or not.
notes.part:C3: Input cap, 0.33 µF as onsemi's sheet shows: keeps the regulator steady when it sits away from C1.
notes.part:C4: Output cap, 0.1 µF as the sheet shows: not needed for stability, but it helps when the load changes quickly.
notes.net:V12: 12 V, steady whatever the circuit draws up to the pump's limit.
